name: MCP Server Templates

hlido_opinion.headline: Explicitly superseded by its own successor — the docs open by telling you to migrate. Reviewed as what it now is: a legacy package with a clear exit path.
hlido_opinion.body: MCP Server Templates offers Docker-powered, zero-configuration deployment of Model Context Protocol servers with a CLI and a template library. The dominant fact about it is announced by the project before anything else: the documentation opens with "This project has evolved into MCP Platform", labels itself Legacy Documentation, and gives the migration in two lines — `pip uninstall mcp-templates && pip install mcp-platform`, then replace `mcpt` with `mcpp` in your commands. We score it as what it is today rather than what it was, and a superseded package is a poor choice for new work no matter how sound the original design. That said, the deprecation is handled about as well as deprecations get: the successor is named, linked and documented; the migration is two commands rather than a rewrite; the legacy docs remain published instead of being deleted out from under existing users; and the naming change is explained rather than just imposed. Some content is visibly stale — a features section still headed "Mid-August 2025 Release" — and the modest repository signals (21 stars, 5 forks on the captured page) suggest this never reached wide adoption before moving on. Anyone landing here should follow the project's own advice and go to MCP Platform; the reason to record this entry at all is so that agents and people who find the legacy package know it is legacy.

tier_rationale: FADING (48) because the project itself declares it superseded on the first line of its own documentation and directs readers to MCP Platform. The deprecation is handled well — successor named and linked, two-command migration, legacy docs left in place — which keeps it from scoring lower, but a package whose maintainer says to install something else cannot be recommended for new work. Confidence is medium rather than low here: the central finding is stated unambiguously by the vendor.
what_it_does_well: Deprecation is announced clearly and immediately rather than left for users to discover
Successor (MCP Platform) is named, linked, and separately documented
Migration is genuinely two commands, not a rewrite: uninstall/install, then mcpt → mcpp
Legacy documentation is left published rather than deleted, so existing users are not stranded
The rename is explained (better reflects the platform's capabilities) rather than imposed silently
Original design is sound — Docker-powered zero-configuration deployment with a real CLI and template library
what_it_fails_at: Superseded by MCP Platform — the vendor's own first instruction is to migrate away
Content is visibly stale, including a features section still headed 'Mid-August 2025 Release'
Modest repository signals (21 stars, 5 forks on the captured page) suggest limited adoption before the move
No security or maintenance commitment stated for the legacy package now that the successor exists
Anything learned here has to be re-learned against MCP Platform's documentation
best_for: Existing mcp-templates users who need the legacy reference while migrating
Anyone tracing why a `mcpt` command in an old runbook no longer matches current documentation
not_recommended_for: New projects — use MCP Platform, as the vendor instructs
Production deployments needing an actively maintained package with a security commitment
Anyone evaluating MCP deployment tooling for the first time

red_flags.note: The package is superseded. Its own documentation opens by telling readers to migrate to MCP Platform. Flagged so that anyone (or any agent) arriving at the legacy docs from a search result does not adopt it by mistake.

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: A CLI and templates for deploying MCP servers — infrastructure an agent ends up running behind, not a surface an agent calls. New integrations should target MCP Platform instead.
